target: Cyn gwneud dim, meddylia.
tip: 'cyn' (before) takes the verb-noun straight on: 'cyn gwneud' = before doing. No 'ing', just the base verb.

target: Daeth brawd fy ffrind.
tip: Possession is two nouns side by side, with no 'of': 'brawd fy ffrind' = my friend's brother.

target: Ga i bwdin, plis?
tip: 'ga i' (may I have) softens the word after it: 'pwdin' turns into 'bwdin'. 'ga i bwdin' = can I have dessert.

target: Anfonwyd y llythyr ddoe.
tip: The '-wyd' ending makes a past with no stated doer: 'anfonwyd y llythyr' = the letter was sent.

target: Siaradodd hi â'r athro.
tip: 'siarad â' means to speak to: 'siaradodd hi â'r athro' = she spoke to the teacher. 'â' marks who is addressed.

target: Does dim gardd ganddyn nhw.
tip: Welsh has no verb 'to have'. 'gan' carries it: 'ganddyn nhw' = they have. 'does dim gardd ganddyn nhw' = they have no garden.

target: Ddaeth e ddim â'i gôt.
tip: To bring is 'dod â' (come with), so it needs 'â': 'ddaeth e ddim â'i gôt' = he didn't bring his coat.

target: Wnaeth e ddim mwynhau'r cyngerdd.
tip: Past negatives often use 'gwneud' (do) as a helper: 'wnaeth e ddim mwynhau' = he didn't enjoy. The main verb stays as the base 'mwynhau'.

target: Aeth y bws hebdda i.
tip: Prepositions take personal endings: 'heb' (without) plus me becomes 'hebdda i' = without me.

target: Dw i eisiau dringo'r Wyddfa.
tip: Want to do something is 'eisiau' plus the verb-noun, with no word for 'to': 'dw i eisiau dringo' = I want to climb.

target: Dylen ni drio'r bwyty newydd.
english: We should try the new restaurant.
tip: 'dylen ni' means we should (a form of 'dylwn'). No 'yn' follows, the verb comes straight after: 'dylen ni drio' = we should try.

target: Dydyn ni ddim wedi gorffen eto.
tip: 'wedi' before a verb makes the 'have done' form: 'wedi gorffen' = have finished. Wrap it with 'ddim' to negate.

target: Faswn i ddim yn gwneud hynny.
tip: 'faswn i' = I would, the 'would' form of 'bod'. Add 'ddim' for the negative: 'faswn i ddim' = I wouldn't.

target: Mynnodd e ei fod e'n iawn.
tip: Report 'that he' with 'ei fod e': 'mynnodd e ei fod e'n iawn' = he insisted that he was right.

target: Fydd dim cyfarfod yr wythnos hon.
english: There won't be a meeting this week.
tip: The future 'bydd' often softens to 'fydd' in negatives: 'fydd dim cyfarfod' = there won't be a meeting.

target: Gobeithio y caf i'r cyfle i ddiolch.
english: I hope I get the opportunity to thank you.
tip: 'caf i' means I will get, an irregular future of 'cael' (to get, receive): 'gobeithio y caf i' = I hope I get.

target: Dw i angen prynu bara a llaeth heddiw.
english: I need to buy bread and milk today.
tip: Need to do something is 'angen' plus the verb-noun, nothing between: 'dw i angen prynu' = I need to buy.

target: Mae'r meddyg yn dweud bod rhaid i fi orffwys.
english: The doctor says I need to rest.
tip: 'rhaid i' plus a person plus verb-noun means must: 'rhaid i fi orffwys' = I must rest, literally 'necessity to me to rest'.

target: Dw i ddim wedi bod at y deintydd eleni.
english: I haven't been to the dentist this year.
tip: For going to a person, use 'at' rather than 'i': 'at y deintydd' = to the dentist. 'i' is usually for places, 'at' for people.

target: Mae'r gymuned yma'n gyfeillgar a chroesawgar iawn.
english: This community is very friendly and welcoming.
tip: The linking word 'a' (and) triggers aspirate mutation, adding an h-sound: 'croesawgar' becomes 'chroesawgar' after 'a'.

target: Croeso i Gymru, gobeithio byddwch chi'n mwynhau!
english: Welcome to Wales, I hope you'll enjoy it!
tip: 'byddwch chi' = you will, for a group or a polite 'you': 'gobeithio byddwch chi'n mwynhau' (hope you'll enjoy).

target: Aeth Megan â'r plant i'r pwll nofio.
english: Megan took the children to the swimming pool.
tip: 'mynd â' means to take, literally go with: 'aeth Megan â'r plant' = Megan took the children.

target: Dyw e ddim wedi bod yng Nghymru o'r blaen.
english: He hasn't been to Wales before.
tip: 'yn' meaning in triggers nasal mutation and shifts to 'yng': 'Cymru' becomes 'Nghymru', giving 'yng Nghymru' = in Wales.

target: Pe gallwn i goginio fel hi, byddwn i'n agor bwyty.
english: If I could cook like her, I'd open a restaurant.
tip: 'pe gallwn i' means if I could, the 'could' form of 'gallu' (to be able): 'pe gallwn i goginio' (if I could cook).

target: Cwrddais i â ffrind.
tip: 'cwrdd' takes the linker 'â' for the person you meet: 'cwrddais i â ffrind' (I met a friend).

target: Trowch i'r chwith wrth y goleuadau.
tip: 'trowch' is a command with the '-wch' ending, used for a group or someone formal. To a single friend you'd say 'tro'.

target: Aeth y bachgen bach i gysgu.
english: The little boy went to sleep.
tip: 'mynd' (to go) is irregular in the past: 'aeth' = went, not 'mynddodd'. 'aeth y bachgen' = the boy went.

target: Roedd yn well ganddo de na choffi.
tip: Preference is shown with 'gan': 'roedd yn well ganddo' = he preferred it, literally it was better with him.

target: Gwyddai hi fod y gwaith yn anodd.
english: She knew the work was hard.
tip: In reported speech, that is carried by 'fod', a softened 'bod': 'gwyddai hi fod y gwaith' = she knew that the work was hard.

target: Roedd hi'n arfer chwarae'r piano bob nos.
english: She used to play the piano every evening.
tip: 'yn arfer' plus a verb means used to as a habit: 'roedd hi'n arfer chwarae' = she used to play.
